output.brief: First-contact resolution fell mainly because of the Finance credit-limit change on 14 April, not the new starters. The agent credit limit dropped from £100 to £25, and larger adjustments now go automatically to the Billing Resolution team. The share of billing calls referred rose from 7% to 54% in the week the change went live. Referred calls resolve at about 33%, against 82% for the rest, and those rates did not change. Experienced agents fell by the same amount as the April intake, and referral rates were similar across tenure groups. The tariff mix and the IVR redesign (which came later than the first drop) don't explain the fall. I'm fairly confident, though I did not collect direct evidence on workload or the IVR. Don't put April-intake agents on performance plans: the evidence doesn't support blaming them, and the plan would punish the wrong people. Next, agree a revised in-call credit limit with Finance, backed by post-call sampling. Trial it on two teams for six weeks, tracking FCR and unsupported credits, before rolling out wider. The limit can be changed in a day. Also ask MI to run the reason and referral breakdown routinely.
